title: The names peanuts hide behind
standfirst: Peanuts goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name peanuts when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to peanuts is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to peanut is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 10 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA), Public Law 108-282, Title II — peanuts listed as a major food allergen; highly refined peanut oil exempt (21 U.S.C. 321(qq))
FASTER Act of 2021 (Public Law 117-11) — reaffirms peanut as a major food allergen (adds sesame as the 9th)
Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, Annex II — 'Peanuts and products thereof'
Peanut Allergy — 'Avoiding Peanut' hidden-names list (mandelona, goober, monkey nuts, beer nuts, artificial nuts, Nu-Nuts, mixed nuts, arachis oil, HVP)

International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients — Arachis Hypogaea (Peanut) Oil / Seed Oil / Seedcake / Flour

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not peanuts. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
